patch_description:
The current program uses 34 long single-point annealing restarts (5350 iterations each), with initial scale 0.125, final scale 0.0075, and active-triangle-biased moves. This is robust but expensive and has limited coordinated population-level exploration.

The new implementation uses normalized affine determinants directly, reducing repeated Cartesian conversion. It replaces most serial annealing with six deterministic differential-evolution islands using population size 120 and 340 generations. The first three islands use fresh structured/simplex populations; later islands use archive-seeded restarts, perturbing prior elite configurations while retaining some fresh samples. Selection prioritizes strict minimum determinant while using a small lower-tail score only for near ties. A final 760-round active-set batch polish uses 176 coordinated candidates per round, concentrating moves on points involved in the 18 smallest triangle constraints. This combines broad exploration, archive transfer, and targeted local repair.
